newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel lower against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel lower against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened against the dollar on Thursday in thin trading following the rise of the U.S. currency against the mark, dealers said.

"Trading was very quiet today and the session opened with slightly more conversions of dollars into shekels. When the shekel reached 3.5120 shekels per dollar the trend changed and the shekel started declining," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank.
"The only evident reason for the shekel's decline is the rise of the dollar against the mark," she said.
The dollar rose in Europe on Thursday to a new six-year high against the mark topping 1.83 marks for the first time since August 1991.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5220 shekels compared with 3.5140 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7767 against 3.7729 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.0434 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.0517 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 1.9202 shekels compared with 1.9207 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5240 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233S
